title: Material properties vocabulary
keyIdea: Use exact words in pairs: transparent/translucent/opaque, conductor/insulator, soluble/insoluble, flexible/rigid, magnetic/non-magnetic.

kid: Scientists use exact words for properties. Transparent means you can see clearly through it. Translucent lets some light through, but things look blurry. Opaque lets no light through.

There are more words in pairs. A conductor lets heat or electricity through, and an insulator does not. Soluble means it dissolves, and insoluble means it does not. Flexible means it bends, and rigid means it does not.
adult: Precise words make comparisons clear: 'thermal insulator' says more than 'keeps warm'. Pair each word with its opposite: conductor/insulator, soluble/insoluble, flexible/rigid, magnetic/non-magnetic.
Use the words to justify a choice. A window needs a transparent, rigid, waterproof material, so glass is used. A tea cosy needs a flexible thermal insulator, so wool or fabric works.

familyTip: Shine a torch through things at home: a glass, a tissue, a book. Name each one: transparent, translucent or opaque.

practice.prompt: Frosted glass lets light through, but you can't see clearly through it. It is…
practice.explain: Some light gets through but the view is blurred: translucent.
Insoluble means it does not dissolve.

practice.prompt: Out of {n} materials, {k} are opaque. How many let at least some light through?
practice.hint: Opaque ones let no light through.

practice.prompt: {a} g of soluble sugar is stirred into {b} g of water. What is the total mass, in grams?

pool.prompt: A tea cosy should be made of a…
pool.explain: It must stop heat escaping: a thermal insulator.
Rigid is the opposite of flexible.

pool.prompt: A test found {k} of {n} metals were magnetic. How many were non-magnetic?
{a} g of insoluble sand is stirred into {b} g of water, then filtered out. What mass of sand is caught in the filter, in grams?
pool.explain: All {a} g of sand is caught.

visual.caption: Hold each material in the torch beam. How much light reaches the screen?
